Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

double adjective and noun

twice as much; made of two

also twice as much, twice as many, twofold, as much again, the double, twice the size

classical

Phaedr. 1 prol. 3: duplex libellī dōs est
Caes. B.G. 2.29.3: duplicī altissimō mūrō (Lewis & Short)

duplex, duplicis

adjective, third declension, one ending

double, twofold: made of two, or having two parts

Of a thing made of two or with two parts: a double wall, a double gift. Of character it means two-faced, deceitful: duplex Ulixēs (Hor. C. 1.6.7, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • duplus, dupla, duplum — twice as much, twice as large

    adjective; as a noun, duplum, duplī n., the double · classical · Liv. 29.19: dupla pecūnia (Lewis & Short); Cato Agr. praef. 1: fūrem duplī condemnārī (Lewis & Short)

    Of amounts and prices: duplum, twice the sum; in duplum, twofold; duplō major, twice as big (Plin.). Duplex says what a thing is made of, duplus how much there is.

  • alterum tantum — as much again, twice as much

    phrase: alter and the neuter of tantus · also used · classical · Plaut. Epid. 518–519: etiam sī alterum tantum perdundumst; Cic. Or. 188: partem pedis aut aequālem esse alterī partī aut alterō tantō aut sēsqui esse majōrem, one part of a foot equal to the other, or twice as long, or half as long again

    Where English doubles, Latin often counts “the same amount a second time”.

Examples

  • duplex libellī dōs est: quod rīsum movet et quod prūdentī vītam cōnsiliō monet

    the little book’s gift is double: it makes you laugh, and it guides your life with wise advicePhaedr. 1 prol. 3–4

  • ingeniī signum in parvīs praecipuum memoria est. ejus duplex virtūs, facile percipere et fidēliter continēre

    in little ones the chief sign of talent is memory; and its strength is double: to take things in easily and to keep them faithfullyQuint. 1.3.1

  • immō etiam sī alterum tantum perdundumst, perdam potius quam sinam mē impūne irrīsum esse

    no: even if I have to lose as much again, I’d rather lose it than let them laugh at me and get away with itPlaut. Epid. 518–520

See also double, twice, half, pair.
